title: 11 Dead, 181 Hospitalised After Suspected Spurious Liquor in Manipur's Chandel District
excerpt: Deaths over three days in Chakpikarong subdivision are linked to liquor reportedly bought in Sugnu; doctors suspect methanol poisoning as the chief minister orders an enquiry and hospitals in Imphal treat 181 patients.
body:
• At least 11 people have died and 181 have been hospitalised in Manipur's Chandel district over three days after allegedly consuming spurious liquor, officials said on Friday, November 20, 2026.
  • Doctors suspect methanol poisoning, but officials say the exact cause of the deaths has not yet been medically established and remains under investigation.
  • Police say the liquor the victims consumed was reportedly purchased from Sugnu in neighbouring Kakching district; Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh has ordered an enquiry.
  • The Chandel district administration has warned residents not to drink locally brewed liquor or alcohol of doubtful origin, and says anyone with vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision or breathing difficulty after drinking should seek medical care immediately.

At least 11 people have died and 181 others have been hospitalised over the past three days in Manipur's Chandel district, allegedly after consuming spurious liquor, officials said on Friday. The deaths were reported between November 18 and 20 in the Chakpikarong subdivision and adjoining areas of the hill district, which shares an unfenced border with Myanmar.

According to a police official, the first victim, 50-year-old Hrangbung Beruwng Anal, died at his home in Nungpan village on Wednesday night. Ten more people died on Thursday and Friday in villages across the district, several of them while being taken to hospital or at local primary and community health centres.

Hospitals under strain in Imphal

Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh confirmed the toll and said more than 140 patients were undergoing treatment at Shija Hospital in Lamphelpat, while another 41 had been admitted to Babina Hospital in Sajiwa. Dr Chetan Khundongbam, joint managing director of Shija Hospital, said the hospital had received around 140 patients suspected of methanol poisoning, most of them from the Chakpikarong area. Three patients were in critical condition and undergoing haemodialysis, he told ANI.

Singh visited both hospitals on Friday, met doctors and patients, and assured government support for those under treatment. He directed officials to conduct an enquiry to identify those responsible, said the culprits would be arrested soon, and sent a medical team including specialists in general medicine to Chandel district.

Liquor traced to Sugnu, cause not yet confirmed

Chandel Superintendent of Police Dharmendra Kumar, in a report to Deputy Commissioner Mamoni Doley, said the adulterated liquor reportedly consumed by the victims had been purchased from Sugnu in neighbouring Kakching district. Officials stressed that the exact cause of the deaths is yet to be medically and scientifically established and remains under investigation, and that laboratory findings confirming the substance involved have not yet been released. Doctors treating the patients suspect methanol, a highly toxic form of alcohol that can cause severe illness and death when present in illicitly made liquor.

Advisory: what residents should do

The Chandel district administration has issued a seven-point advisory as a precaution. Residents are strongly advised to refrain from consuming locally brewed liquor or alcoholic beverages of doubtful origin, particularly from suspected sources in the affected areas, until further notice. The advisory says anyone experiencing vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, breathing difficulty or other unusual symptoms after consuming alcohol should immediately seek medical attention at the nearest health facility — advice that matters because methanol poisoning can worsen quickly, and early treatment improves the chances of recovery.

Hooch tragedies recur across India despite enforcement drives, typically when methanol is mixed into or contaminates illicitly distilled liquor sold cheaply in areas where legal supply is limited or expensive. In Chandel, officials said there was no known local brewing or manufacture of local wine, which is why the investigation is focused on the supply traced to Sugnu. The state government says the enquiry will identify those responsible for the supply; further official updates on the toll and the laboratory findings are awaited.
